title: Ctrl-C recorded as task failure
grade_detail: patch_apply: git apply failed: error: b/runner.py: No such file or directory; fuzzy: no hunks applied (skipped=['runner.py@18'])

answer.patch:
--- a/runner.py
+++ b/runner.py
@@ -18,4 +18,4 @@
         tid = task["id"]
         try:
             row = run_one(task)
-        except BaseException as e:   # noqa: BLE001
+        except Exception as e:
             row = {
answer.reason: KeyboardInterrupt inherits from BaseException, so the except block swallows Ctrl-C, records a failure row, and continues instead of terminating. Changing to Exception allows KeyboardInterrupt (and SystemExit) to propagate, stopping the process cleanly without leaving a scored failure row.

title: Chat timeout_s never reaches HTTP client

answer.patch:
--- a/chat/wrap.py
+++ b/chat/wrap.py
@@ -15,13 +15,13 @@ def chat_wrapped(
     timeout_s: float | None = None,
     temperature: float = 0.1,
     max_tokens: int = 1024,
     retry: int = 1,
 ) -> dict[str, Any]:
-    del timeout_s
     last: dict[str, Any] | None = None
     for _ in range(max(1, retry)):
         last = api.post_chat(
             model,
             messages,
+            timeout_s=timeout_s,
             temperature=temperature,
             max_tokens=max_tokens,
          )
answer.reason: In chat/wrap.py, the `timeout_s` parameter was explicitly deleted (`del timeout_s`) and never forwarded to `api.post_chat()`, causing the HTTP layer to always receive the default `None`. The fix removes the deletion and passes `timeout_s=timeout_s` to the API call.

title: Timed-out child with stderr-only output loses diagnostics

answer.patch:
--- a/util/subprocess_timeout.py
+++ b/util/subprocess_timeout.py
@@ -56,4 +56,4 @@
         proc.wait(timeout=10)
         stdout = e.stdout if e.stdout else ""
         stderr = e.stderr if e.stderr else ""
-        if str(stdout).strip():
+        if stdout or stderr:
             return subprocess.CompletedProcess(
answer.reason: The timeout handler only returned a CompletedProcess when stdout had content, silently raising ProcTimeout when the subprocess only wrote to stderr. Changed the condition to check for any output (stdout or stderr) so callers always receive the killed process result with the stderr dump.

title: Warmup ignores short timeout

answer.patch:
--- a/warmup.py
+++ b/warmup.py
@@ -9,5 +9,4 @@
 
 
 def warmup(model: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
-     _ = config.FIRST_BYTE_S
-     return chat(model, "Reply with exactly: OK")
+    return chat(model, "Reply with exactly: OK", timeout_s=config.DEFAULT_WARMUP_TIMEOUT_S)
